title: Stratified sampling and population weighting
outcome: Estimate a declared target mixture from an intentionally balanced evaluation and diagnose overlap and weight concentration.

exercises.title: Change the mixture
exercises.task: Use 25% routine and 75% rare in case A.
exercises.hint: Multiply each mean by its target weight.
exercises.answer: 0.25(0.9)+0.75(0.5)=0.6. The model outcomes are unchanged; only the target population differs.

exercises.title: Expose missing support
exercises.task: Give positive target weight to an unobserved stratum.
exercises.hint: Missing support cannot be repaired with normalization.
exercises.answer: The outcome mean for that stratum is unidentified without additional data or explicit modeling assumptions.

exercises.title: Compare denominators
exercises.task: Explain why the two weighted means in case B differ.
exercises.expected: \(0.2\) uses the known population size \(N=10\); \(1/3\) uses the sampled weight sum \(6\).
exercises.answer: Horvitz-Thompson estimates the population total before dividing by N. Self-normalization divides by an estimated total weight and need not equal it.

exercises.title: Increase weight concentration
exercises.answer: A nominal sample of two is dominated by one weighted observation. ESS describes concentration but does not replace a clustering analysis.

exercises.title: Audit zero probability
exercises.task: Set one inclusion probability to zero.
exercises.answer: An event that cannot enter the sample cannot provide an observed outcome for this estimator.

exercises.title: Compare systems fairly
exercises.task: Use a common family/stratum ledger to compare A and B.
exercises.expected: Both estimates use identical eligible IDs and target weights.
exercises.answer: Paired, consistently weighted differences prevent a traffic-mixture change from masquerading as a model improvement.
